preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner
Contract must have accumulated BNB from taxes

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the sweepContingency() function before liquidity is added to drain all BNB from the contract to the owner's address. Alternatively, after liquidity is added, use manualDeposit() to send contract BNB to the reflector contract, then manipulate the reflector to extract funds. The owner can also set tax wallets to their own addresses to receive all tax distributions.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has owner-only functions that allow draining of contract BNB. The sweepContingency() function transfers all BNB to the owner but only works before liquidity is added (_hasLiqBeenAdded == false). Since the contract starts with _hasLiqBeenAdded = false, and the owner can call this function, we can drain any accumulated BNB from taxes.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner, ensure the contract has BNB balance (simulating tax accumulation), then call sweepContingency() to drain all BNB to the owner address (which we control).
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner address from the contract. 2. Start prank as the owner. 3. Use deal() to give the contract some BNB (simulating tax accumulation). 4. Call sweepContingency() as owner. 5. Verify attacker balance increased.
